title: Co-leading a band with Illinois Jacquet and writing Robin's Nest
summary: After the Hawkins bookings ended he and Jacquet organized a short-lived band in San Diego, and in New York in 1947 they collaborated on Robin's Nest.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: That was about 1946. I think sometimes I forget to really pinpoint these years, but then you led a band -- co-led a band with Illinois Jacquet, 1947-48.

Well, during the time I was playing with Coleman Hawkins which was after I played with Lucky Millinder, when I got to California as I said, the bookings sort of petered out and rather than to continue on the road with these uncertainties, I got together with Illinois Jacquet, who we had played together, we had played together with Lionel Hampton, and we organized a band together. We played in San Diego -- San Diego, yes. We played a job in San Diego. It didn't last too long, but we had Henry Coker on trombone and Oscar Pettiford on bass --

And his brother, Russell Jacquet on trumpet. But this didn't last too long because we didn't have any bookings and so forth, and I went back to New York and continued on with my association and then we got together again in New York when he later came there, and I collaborated with him in playing and arranging and writing some music, out of which came my composition 'Robin's Nest'. That was in 1947.
